name: Moving spare network cables
brief:
An office has `n` machines, numbered 0 to `n - 1`, and a list of `cables`. Each cable is a pair `(a, b)` joining two different machines, and two machines can talk when a chain of cables links them. A technician may unplug any cable and plug it in again between any two machines.

Write `spare_cable_moves(n, cables)`, which returns the fewest cables to move so that every machine can talk to every other, or -1 if there are too few cables.

Example. With `n = 4` and cables `(0, 1)`, `(0, 2)`, `(1, 2)`, machine 3 is alone. The cable `(1, 2)` is spare, since 1 and 2 still talk through 0, and moving it to reach 3 gives the answer 1.
constraints: $1 \le n \le 200{,}000$ and $0 \le$ `len(cables)` $\le 200{,}000$. The same pair may appear more than once.
$O(n + m)$ time for $m$ cables is the target. Recursion deep enough for a long chain of machines will fail in Python.
Each test has its own 5-second limit in the browser.
hint: Linking `c` separate groups takes `c - 1` cables. When there are at least `n - 1` cables, some group always holds enough spares. So count the groups.

examples.note: Two groups, {0, 1, 2} and {3}, and the cable (1, 2) is spare.
Six machines need at least five cables, and there are four.

tests.call: spare_cable_moves(200000, [(i, i + 1) for i in range(199999)])

how: Submit runs 12 hidden tests. Each answer must equal the expected value.
notes: Count the connected groups `c`; with at least `n - 1` cables there are always `c - 1` spare ones, so the answer is `c - 1`.
The cable count decides -1 before any search, and a recursive walk breaks on a chain of 200,000 machines, so keep an explicit stack.
Building the lists and one walk over every machine and cable is $O(n + m)$.
